author: Nineteenth century videos. Back to life.
description:
While the world rushes toward a new century of steel and speed, a small group of children reminds us of what never changes.

In this rare glimpse of the Belle Époque, we step away from the grand boulevards to find a moment of pure, quiet joy. Surrounded by the cobblestones of a city in transition, these babies and toddlers play with a simplicity that feels almost sacred. Notice their oversized caps and the heavy fabrics of their Sunday best, a stark contrast to the modern traffic of horse-drawn carriages and early trams humming in the background.

There is a haunting beauty in the way they look into the camera. To them, this lens was a strange, new invention; to us, it is a miracle that allows us to reach across 130 years. As Claude Debussy’s "La plus que lente" drifts through the scene, the slow, melancholic waltz mirrors the gentle pace of their play, capturing the fragile elegance of a moment that exists now only in these moving shadows.

Music: Claude Debussy, La plus que lente.
title: (1896, 4K, 60fps) A day in XIX Century life.
